ratings_why.fun: Four real builds and a play-order puzzle every turn, with Gust Pages giving clean early tempo; held back from 8 because permanent growth is thin from Tier 3 to 5 before the Tower spikes.
ratings_why.distinct: Late turns the hand into a second board that lands mid-fight, out of reach of enemy Start of Combat; no Battlegrounds tribe fights from the hand, which is what lifts it over a 7.

verdict_why: Two cards don't work as written (the Couriers and Lady High Pressure's held Gusts); fix those and it can settle.

points.text: The Swift Couriers 'can't be placed on the board' yet arrive Late into a slot, and 'your unit nearest it' has no reference point. Say whether they take a slot and fight, and nearest to what.
Lady High Pressure doesn't say what happens to a held Gust whose unit died before the Storm, or whether held Late units still count toward her sixth attack. State both.
Permanent growth is capped small from Tier 3 to 5 (Föhn, Heron, Black Cloud), then the Tower jumps to 50-100 a turn. A Tier 5 permanent scaler for the Late build would keep mid-game boards climbing.
Keeper of the Glass is the only gold card and only pays after a big Gust fight. A second economy piece tied to Late arrivals would help the Late build tier up on time.

standouts.why: Duke Cumulonimbus counting the gap is a great payoff, and it gives Black Cloud and Lady High Pressure a real tradeoff.
Sir Vane makes play order a decision every turn, and he ties the Gust and Late halves together.
Lady High Pressure holding everything and then releasing it doubled is a capstone you build a whole game toward.

weakest.why: Windhover gains +1/+1 once a fight, which falls off fast and doesn't grow with the tribe.
Mr Fair's swap is fiddly for what it gives, and the End of Turn buff is generic.
Keeper of the Glass pays little and only when you're already winning fights with Gusts.

flags.note: The Tower of the Winds at 8 faces gives +8/+8 to every board unit, over 100 stats a turn, and double that golden. Near the guide's top, and Late units count as faces.
Lady High Pressure with the Steward is x4 Gusts, x9 with goldens; one-sided wipes, plus feel-bad stalls if a wide enemy kills you before the sixth attack.
The Master of the Wild Hunt with Black Cloud gives every revived unit a permanent +2/+2 each fight; bounded by deaths but it repeats every fight.
The Swift Couriers: 'never lands' conflicts with arriving in a slot, and 'nearest it' is undefined.
